reasoning: Identity (EO 12047, 1978-03-27, Carter, 43 FR 13359, filed 1978-03-28, printed 1978-03-29), the six-clause inventory, all quotes and hashes check out. The operative analysis of secs 1, 2, 3 and 5 is supported: EO 12388 (effective as of 1982-08-24) only substitutes the agency name, the 22 U.S.C. 2459 note lists no other amendment, the FR note shows only the EO 12388 amendment and the EO 11312 revocation, no held order text revokes it, and the 2026-10-02 State Department notice makes the sec 1 determinations under EO 12047. But the first_end of both terminated clauses (sec 4 revocation of EO 11312 and sec 6 effective-date clause) is dated 1975-04-01, which contradicts the source (effective April 1, 1978), the claim's own reasons (1978-04-01) and is three years before the order was signed. A wrong first-end date on a terminated clause is a defect requiring rejection even though the whole-order YES outcome is unaffected.

reasoning: Identity matches (1961-12-05, Kennedy, 26 FR 11714, printed 1961-12-07). The eight-clause inventory covers every operative section and subsection. The order has no duration, condition or deadline; the FR catalog (complete past the cutoff) records no amendment, revocation or supersession; the number search of held order texts finds only the order, the 1989 codification (unamended) and the 2011 Commerce notice showing the program running; USC and eCFR searches through the cutoff have no hit. The predicate therefore rests on the order's continuing terms plus bounded searches for an ending rather than on a positive 2026 source, and the claim says exactly that, which resolves the empty-catalog flag honestly; an endpoint would need a reason and none is shown. Upheld on that basis. Non-blocking wording note: sec6 judgment calls the pin a 'lapel pin'; the text says 'a suitably designed pin inscribed with the President's "E"'.
